  "narrative": "Validation of H13 (CRP >= 10) is now assessed. The discovery estimate was +0.452 log-months (CI [0.440, 0.464]) and the independent validation (R24) yielded +0.458 log-months (CI [0.440, 0.475]). Both estimates are highly consistent, exceeding the 0.21 log-month clinical significance threshold by a factor of ~2.2. The effect is robust across independent samples, confirming CRP >= 10 as a strong prognostic marker. H13 is accepted.\n\nThe convergence of H6 (NLR >= 3), H13 (CRP >= 10), and H21 (Stage IV) at ~0.45 log-months remains a critical concern. While these represent distinct biological axes (neutrophil inflammation, systemic inflammation, disease burden), their identical magnitude suggests a potential shared confound or a 'sick patient' phenotype where these factors co-occur. However, the independent validation of H13 supports the robustness of the inflammatory axis. Further investigation into interactions (e.g., CRP x NLR) will help disentangle whether these are independent signals or redundant proxies.\n\nInvalid continuous claims (H11, H16, H17, H23) failed due to zero cell counts for exposed=1.0/comparator=0.0. I propose refinements using clinically relevant thresholds (median or specific cut-offs) to enable valid comparisons. Specifically:\n- H11 (NLR): Refine to NLR >= 3 vs < 3 (already tested in H6, but this formalizes the continuous-to-binary bridge).\n- H16 (LDH): Refine to LDH >= median (210.67) vs < median.\n- H17 (Albumin): Refine to Albumin >= median (3.8) vs < median.\n- H23 (Hemoglobin): Refine to Hemoglobin >= median (12.5) vs < median.\n- H8 (Research Signature A): Refine to top quartile (>0.68) vs rest to test for any prognostic signal in the constructed assay.\n\nThese refinements will allow us to assess the graded nature of these prognostic factors and determine if they provide additional information beyond the binary inflammatory markers.",
  "research_notes": "Iteration 2 synthesize. H13 accepted with validation (0.458). H6/H13/H21 convergence (~0.45) noted; likely shared 'sick patient' phenotype or confound, but H13 validated independently. Invalid continuous claims (H11, H16, H17, H23) require binary/median refinements. Proposed refinements for NLR, LDH, Albumin, Hemoglobin, and Research Signature A. Next: analyze these refinements and CRP x NLR interaction."
